reports.title: ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE SEPTEMBER QUARTER 2026 RESULTS AND

desk.period: September quarter 2026 (Q2 fiscal 2027, quarter to 30 Sep 2026)
desk.headline: Revenue up 10% to RMB271.5bn, slightly above estimates; adjusted EPS of RMB8.10 per ADS well below estimates; cloud up 53%

other.label: AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue

results: Revenue grew 10% to RMB271.5bn, just above the RMB269.8bn estimate; adjusted EPS of RMB8.10 per ADS rose 86% but was far below the RMB11.03 estimate.
Cloud revenue jumped 53% to RMB61.0bn, with sales to outside customers up 64%; the unit's adjusted EBITA more than doubled to RMB8.8bn.
E-commerce profit (adjusted EBITA) rose to RMB38.9bn from RMB11.3bn as quick-commerce losses shrank, though China customer management revenue fell 5%.
Losses in the AI Labs and Applications unit widened to RMB10.5bn from RMB3.4bn on model and Qwen app spending.
Capex rose 60% to RMB50.5bn, leaving free cash flow at an outflow of RMB34.5bn; cash and liquid investments stood at RMB487.9bn.

guidance.summary: The results release gives no financial guidance. On the call, the CEO said cloud revenue growth could be 30–45% next year, with new US export controls on compute a possible drag.

items.period: Next year (as stated on the call)

points: CEO Eddie Wu said 2030 targets of US$100bn external cloud revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin remain on track.
He said new US compute export rules will affect next year's products and services, and the impact is still being assessed.
Management expects 2027 and 2028 to be the tightest years for compute supply in China, which may affect next year's plan.
Cloud growth was put at 30–45% next year, rebounding to 50% or more in 2028.
The release notes capex is aimed at AI demand, while the finance chief stressed returns on capital and a goal of positive free cash flow.
call.source: Results announcement (Exhibit 99.1) and call coverage: Reuters via RTÉ, 19 Nov 2026
